title: Mapping-complex presentation of an enriched model localization
statement:
Let $\mathcal M$ be a complete and cocomplete locally presentable category enriched, tensored and cotensored over unbounded complexes of abelian groups [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose its classes $C,F,W$ form a model structure: $W$ has two-out-of-three; the classes are retract closed; $(C,F\cap W)$ and $(C\cap W,F)$ are weak factorization systems with functorial factorizations and generated by sets. Suppose also that, for $i:A\to B$ in $C$ and $p:X\to Y$ in $F$, the map
$$\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(B,X)\longrightarrow\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(A,X)\times_{\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(A,Y)}\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(B,Y)$$
is a degreewise surjection of complexes, and a quasi-isomorphism if $i$ or $p$ belongs to $W$. An object is cofibrant when its initial map is in $C$, fibrant when its terminal map is in $F$, and bifibrant when both hold. Use enriched localization in the sense of [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal].

The inclusions of the full differential graded subcategories $\mathcal M_c$, $\mathcal M_f$ and $\mathcal M_{cf}$ of cofibrant, fibrant and bifibrant objects induce equivalences after enriched localization at their inherited weak equivalences. The full bifibrant differential graded category, interpreted with its derived chain enrichment, itself presents $\mathcal M[W^{-1}]$. For cofibrant $P$ and fibrant $I$, the complex $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{\mathcal M}(P,I)$ represents its enriched mapping object; these identifications are natural as a bifunctor on $\mathcal M_c^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal M_f$, compatible with composition wherever defined. This bifunctor sends weak equivalences in either variable to quasi-isomorphisms. Thus for functorial cofibrant and fibrant replacements $QX\to X$ and $Y\to TY$, a model for the derived mapping object is $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(QX,TY)$. The localized inclusion equivalences and these comparison bifunctors identify different choices with coherent natural equivalences; an enriched choice of the replacement functors is not required.
